A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pseudo-Stereo work. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support matching across the revisions. All nine pages of v1 and ten pages of v2 were inspected; neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original KITTI evaluations, component ablations, convergence curves, and qualitative disparity results in Section IV.

after.justification: v2 retains original KITTI experiments and adds SceneFlow/Spring evaluations with multiple backbones in Section 4.2, Table 2, and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The rendering procedure, occlusion masking and gradient detachment, padding and wider cropping, fully pseudo-stereo inputs, and losses remain unchanged. GMStereo and MonSter are additional evaluation backbones; no new algorithmic adaptation is specified.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates stereo matching on KITTI 2012 and KITTI 2015. v2 additionally evaluates SceneFlow and Spring, with quantitative and qualitative results covering substantially different scenes beyond the retained driving benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds OASM-DDS but removes v1 Table I's supervised DispNetC, PSMNet, and LoS comparisons and dataset-generation MfS-PSMNet, NS-PSMNet, and Rversing-PSMNet comparisons. Figure 6 also adds Flow2Stereo and CRD-Fusion as qualitative comparators, substantially changing comparison coverage.

E3.justification: v2 introduces paired evaluations with and without pseudo-stereo across PSMNet, GMStereo, and MonSter, plus a MonSter KITTI submission. Spring uses half resolution. It also corrects the stated D1 criterion from error below 3 pixels or 5% to error above both thresholds; this does not establish that retained KITTI results were recomputed.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds controlled tests of whether pseudo-stereo remains effective across architectures and datasets, supported by occlusion error maps. Conversely, v2 removes the wider-generation-without-fully-pseudo ablation and its convergence curve from v1 Table II/Figure 7. The qualitative analysis of erroneous ground truth and monocular-label smoothing is replaced by focused occlusion comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, or statistical significance tests. The additional result rows and redrawn convergence curves do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched KITTI scores and retained ablation values are unchanged, including PSMNet's 4.68% KITTI 2015 D1-all. v2 adds a MonSter result of 4.39% under a different backbone setting and new results for six backbone/dataset combinations in Table 2. It removes several comparator results and the ablation reporting 4.11% D1-all and 0.99 EPE.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) remain mathematically unchanged, with no added theorem or proof. However, Section 4.1 corrects the mathematical definition of D1 error from the below-threshold condition stated in v1 to exceeding both the absolute and relative error thresholds.

C1.justification: The central claim that decoupling inputs and feedback addresses persistent occlusions is retained. v2 adds explicit generality across architectures and datasets to its stated contributions and conclusion, while dropping v1's claims of competitiveness with DispNetC and dataset-generation approaches.

C2.justification: v2 substantially revises the discussion of applicability and failure conditions. Beyond v1's brief warning about indistinct colors and interference, it argues that textureless and reflective regions require information beyond binocular cues and develops a multi-frame research direction. It adds the rationale that unlabeled training cannot rely on validation-based early stopping, while removing interpretations attributing competing methods' errors to erroneous labels and monocular distillation.

D1.justification: Core optimizer, crop, batch-size, augmentation, and loss-weight details remain. v2 reports two RTX 4090 GPUs instead of one and specifies half-resolution Spring, but omits v1's code link, explicit all-image-pairs training/validation disclosure, and approximately 35,000-iteration, seven-hour convergence report. These omissions do not establish an actual change to KITTI data usage.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from contrasting direct photometric methods with dataset generation to emphasizing occlusion masking, local disparity regularities, and additional-view feedback. v2 adds positioning around OASM-DDS, multiscopic supervision, GMStereo, MonSter, and novel-view synthesis, while removing the substantial discussion and citations of Reversing and Learning Stereo from Single Images.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The pseudo-image generation subsection moves before the convergence discussion, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around benchmark comparison, generality, and ablation. Much of the underlying method description remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening qualitative example with a geometric motivation diagram, rebuilds Figure 6 with disparity/error maps, and adds Figure 7 and Table 2. Tables are regrouped and resized, and the convergence plot is simplified and restyled within a different document layout. Figure 8 introduces inconsistent caption references: it cites configurations (c)/(f), while its legend shows (a)/(d)/(g).

improvement.justification: The controlled SceneFlow/Spring experiments across three backbones strengthen evidence beyond v1's PSMNet/KITTI evaluation, and the geometric motivation and error maps clarify the central mechanism. These gains are tempered by reduced code and training-protocol disclosure, removal of useful comparisons and an ablation, and the incorrect Figure 8 caption references. The net improvement is useful but limited.
